   10: Unlike `recon` (guided, human-driven) or `query` (read-only lookup),
   11: the agent is given a VOCABULARY of tool calls and uses Claude to:
   12: 
   13:   1. Plan which tools to call and in what order
   14:   2. Call them autonomously (all read-only, all local)
   15:   3. Synthesise what it found into a concrete patch proposal
   16:   4. Show you the diff and ask ONE confirmation question before writing
   17: 
   18: The agent never writes, commits, or modifies anything without your
   19: explicit "yes". One human gate. Everything before that is autonomous.
   20: 
   21: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   22: TOOL VOCABULARY  (PowerShell-equivalent, all local, all read-only)
   23: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   24: 
   25:   get_file(path)
   26:       Read a file's full content.
   27:       PowerShell: Get-Content -Path <path> -Raw
   28: 
   29:   get_file_lines(path)
   30:       Read with 3-digit line numbers prefixed.

53:       Run graphify's AST call-graph query on a .py file: returns matched
   54:       functions/classes + their callers/callees, scored by relevance.
   55:       Equivalent to `pyslick graphify-query <path> <question>`
   56: 
   57:   jsx_check(path)
   58:       Validate JSX/HTML tag matching in a file.
   59:       Returns a list of any mismatched tags, or "OK".
   60: 
   61:   llm_expand(directive)
   62:       If the local LLM is available, expand the directive into extra
   63:       search terms for richer fuzzy matching. Falls back to the directive
   64:       unchanged if no model is present.
   65: 
   66: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   67: FLOW
   68: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   69: 
   70:   1. Send the directive + tool schema to Claude (Anthropic API)
   71:   2. Claude returns a PLAN (which tools to call, why)
   72:   3. Execute each tool call locally (no data leaves your machine)
   73:   4. Feed results back to Claude for synthesis
   74:   5. Claude proposes: file, find_str, replace_str, explanation
   75:   6. Show diff → ONE confirmation → patchit writes it
   76:   7. git checkpoint
   77: 
   78: The tool calls in steps 2-4 loop up to MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS times so the
   79: agent can react to what it finds (e.g. "that file had no className,
   80: let me check the CSS file instead").
   81: 
   82: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   83: LOCAL LLM MODE (no API key)
   84: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   85: 
   86: When no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / NVIDIA_API_KEY is set, the agent falls back
   87: to _run_local_agent(). That function uses intent_vocab.json to route the
   88: query to the right handler — no reasoning required from the 124M model.
   89: 
   90: Intent routing order (first match wins):
   91:   help         → print pyslick command docs
   92:   git          → show git status / push
   93:   list_files   → walk directory, show files + their main symbols
   94:   comments     → show every comment in the matched file
   95:   nearest      → find_nearest_nodes around a line or symbol
   96:   scan_function→ print a named function end-to-end with comments
   97:   graph        → ast_query / graphify call graph
   98:   connect      → cross-file call-graph walk
   99:   file_info    → purpose + key functions + first 3 lines per function
  100:   patch        → fuzzy match → LLM find/replace → diff → confirm
  101: 
  102: The vocab file lives next to this file: intent_vocab.json
